name: Kingdom of Saudi Arabia

areaKm2.note: asOf 2024. Surface area 2,149,690 km2 (AG.SRF.TOTL.K2); low is land area 2,149,690 km2 (AG.LND.TOTL.K2).

population.note: asOf 2025 (World Bank SP.POP.TOTL 36,973,555). Low -1% / high +1.5% for 2026 growth and estimate uncertainty. All residents incl. ~40% foreign nationals.

activePersonnel.note: IISS Military Balance 2026 p.377 as quoted: 257,000 active incl. the National Guard (paramilitary 24,500 excluded). CIA Factbook 2025: ~250,000 (125,000 MoD + 125,000 National Guard).

trainedReserves.note: IISS Military Balance 2026: no organised reserve. High is an educated allowance for recalled retirees and tribal levies.

supportPersonnel.note: Active 257,000 minus infantry P roles (85,000). Covers air force, air defence force, navy, Strategic Missile Force, crews, logistics and staff.

mobilizationRatio.note: About 58% of residents are citizens (World Bank male population 22.3 m vs female 14.6 m reflects the expatriate workforce); ratio applies to the total population but represents roughly 3-6% of citizens, comparable to other volunteer Gulf militaries; analogue: Kuwait 1990-91 (educated judgement).

count.note: Educated guess. Mechanised infantry of the Army (4 armoured + 5 mechanised brigades) and SANG mechanised brigades on Bradley/LAV. (context page: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saudi_Arabian_National_Guard)

quality.note: Rubric 0.75 band: modern Western kit (M2 Bradley, LAV 6.0).

training.note: Rubric 0.5-0.75: all-volunteer professionals; Yemen war (2015-) exposed weak combined-arms skills.

count.note: Educated guess. SANG light/tribal infantry battalions, airborne brigade, Royal Guard, special forces. (context page: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saudi_Arabian_National_Guard)

training.note: Rubric 0.5-0.75: all-volunteer professionals; Yemen war (2015-) exposed weak combined-arms skills.

count.note: Equipment list: M1A2S 575 + M60A3 370 = 945 active; high adds 140 AMX-30 in reserve (list total 1,085). Low allows for Yemen-war losses.

quality.note: Rubric 0.75: M1A2S is a top-tier tank; M60A3 dated.

training.note: Rubric 0.5-0.75: all-volunteer professionals; Yemen war (2015-) exposed weak combined-arms skills.

count.note: Army: M2A2 380 + AMX-10P 380 (mostly stored) + M113 1,190; SANG: LAV II 724 + LAV III 19 + AMX-10P 90+ (SANG article) = ~2,780; 900 LAV 6.0 on order.

training.note: Rubric 0.5-0.75: all-volunteer professionals; Yemen war (2015-) exposed weak combined-arms skills.

count.note: Equipment list: SP howitzers 380 (M109 110, CAESAR 156 with SANG, AMX-30 AuF1 60, PLZ-45 54) + towed 557 + Astros II 77 + M270 (listed 180, likely includes pods) = ~1,200; many towed 105 mm guns stored, hence mid 1,000.

quality.note: Rubric 0.5-0.75: CAESAR, PLZ-45, Astros modern; towed park old.

training.note: Rubric 0.5-0.75: all-volunteer professionals; Yemen war (2015-) exposed weak combined-arms skills.

count.note: RSAF inventory: Typhoon 72 + F-15 family 210 (C/D MSIP II, F-15SR/SA; 21 used for training, 1 lost 2026) = 282. Up to 48 F-35A in a proposed sale approved Sept 2026 (none delivered).

quality.note: Rubric 0.75: F-15SA and Typhoon among the best 4.5-generation types.

training.note: Rubric 0.75 band minus: decade of combat sorties over Yemen, Western training.

count.note: RSAF inventory: Tornado IDS 81 (MLU TS3 2018). Low allows for retirement as F-15SA/Typhoon take over.

Composite of listed inventories (some figures include on-order): Army AH-64D/E 47, UH-60L/M 100, CH-47F 48, OH-58D 15; SANG AH-64 12, UH-60M 24; RSAF Bell 212 22, Bell 412 14; Navy MH-60R 10, AS332 20, AS565 26 = ~338 incl. orders.

quality.note: Rubric 0.75 band: AH-64E, UH-60M, CH-47F modern.

training.note: Rubric 0.5-0.75: all-volunteer professionals; Yemen war (2015-) exposed weak combined-arms skills.

count.note: Educated guess. Wing Loong/CH-4 class MALE drones; the Army equipment list gives 300 Wing Loong II under a local-production partnership, far above confirmed deliveries. (context page: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_equipment_of_the_Saudi_Arabian_Army)
Navy article: Al Riyadh class (La Fayette mod.) 3 + Al Madinah class 4 + Multi-Mission Surface Combatant (Freedom-derived) 4 named = 11; low if the last MMSC hulls are still working up.

quality.note: Rubric 0.5-0.75: Al Riyadh and MMSC modern, Al Madinah 1980s.

training.note: Rubric 0.5-0.75: all-volunteer professionals; Yemen war (2015-) exposed weak combined-arms skills.

count.note: Navy article: Al Jubail (Avante 2200) corvettes 5 + Badr corvettes 4 + Al Siddiq FAC 9 + Al Jawf (Sandown) MCM 3 + HSI32 interceptors 39 = 60; small craft excluded.

training.note: Rubric 0.5-0.75: all-volunteer professionals; Yemen war (2015-) exposed weak combined-arms skills.

count.note: Educated guess. Royal Saudi Strategic Missile Force: Chinese DF-3 (retired?) and reported DF-21 launchers; numbers secret. (context page: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Royal_Saudi_Air_Defence_Force)

Launcher counts on the RSADF article converted at ~4-6 launchers per battery: Shahine 141 (~30), I-HAWK 128 (~21), Crotale 40 (~8), AMX-30SA SPAAG 50 (~8); Patriot PAC-2/3 ~20 batteries and THAAD 1-2 (educated, not on the page) = ~90.

quality.note: Rubric 0.75: Patriot/THAAD intercepted many Houthi and Iranian missiles 2017-26; Shahine/Hawk old.

commandQuality.note: Rubric 0.5: competent staff with Western support, but the Yemen campaign (2015-) showed poor joint coordination.

cohesion.note: Rubric 0.5: split between MoD army and the tribal-loyalty National Guard.

morale.note: Rubric 0.5: homeland under Iranian (2026) and Houthi (Oct 2026) missile/drone attack; limited appetite for ground war.

weapons.note: Anchor 9-10: Western precision munitions (Paveway, Storm Shadow), JDAM; few indigenous systems.

armor.note: Anchor 9: M1A2S composite armour; no APS.

ships.note: Anchor 9: Aster-armed Al Riyadh, Aegis-lite MMSC.

fortification.note: Anchor 9-10: Patriot plus THAAD layered missile defence, hardened bases.

logistics.note: Anchor 9: large airlift (C-130, A330 MRTT), dependent on foreign contractors.

isr.note: Anchor 9: AWACS, commercial/partner satellite imagery, MALE drones.

air.note: Anchor 9-10: F-15SA and Typhoon 4.5 generation, no 5th generation yet.

gdpPerCapita.note: asOf 2025. GDP 1,866,142,685,811 2011 int$ (World Bank NY.GDP.MKTP.PP.KD rebased x 0.8005) / population 36,973,555 = 50,472 2011 int$. Range +/-10%. Corrected 2026-10-29: values x1.0376 because the rebase factor was an arithmetic error (0.8005); the right factor is 0.8306 (FRED GDPDEF, 2017=100: 2011 91.478 / 2021 110.130). Figures quoted above are before the correction.

gdp.note: asOf 2025. World Bank NY.GDP.MKTP.PP.KD (constant 2021 int$) 2,331,221,343,924 x 0.8005 (US GDP deflator 2011/2021) = 1,866,142,685,811 2011 int$. Range +/-10% for PPP benchmark uncertainty and the relative-price drift the rebase ignores. Corrected 2026-10-29: values x1.0376 because the rebase factor was an arithmetic error (0.8005); the right factor is 0.8306 (FRED GDPDEF, 2017=100: 2011 91.478 / 2021 110.130). Figures quoted above are before the correction.

milSpendShare.note: SIPRI via World Bank: 6.48% of GDP in 2025, 6.41% 2024, 5.72% 2022 (low). Among the highest shares worldwide.

industrialShare.note: asOf 2025: industry incl. construction (and hydrocarbons) 43.0% of GDP (NV.IND.TOTL.ZS). Range +/-7% for oil-price swings.

foodSurplus.note: Educated guess. Imports ~80% of food; some dates/dairy/poultry self-sufficiency.

annualCohort.note: asOf 2025. Males reaching military age per year = male population 22,341,396 x share of males aged 15-19 6.128% (SP.POP.1519.MA.5Y) / 5 = 273,797. Male population from SP.POP.TOTL.MA.IN. Males only (conscript-pool convention). Range +/-10% for single-year cohort variation. Includes expatriate youths; Saudi citizens are roughly 60-70% of the 15-19 cohort.

ifv_apc.note: Educated guess. SAMI/local assembly of LAV and Al-Masmak vehicles.

drones.note: Educated guess. Local Wing Loong assembly partnership (KACST).

roadKm.note: asOf 2006: 221,372 km (47,529 paved); dated figure, network has grown (high).

railKm.note: CIA Factbook: 5,410 km (2016) incl. Haramain HSR and North-South line; World Bank 2,939 km (2018) counts only part. Mid follows the Factbook.

majorPorts.note: CIA Factbook 2024: 16 ports, 0 large, 1 medium; 8 key ports named (Dammam, Duba, Jiddah, Jizan, Ju Aymah, Ras Tanura, Ras al Khafji, Ras al Mishab).

merchantTonnage.note: asOf 2025: 17,445 thousand DWT under the Saudi flag (9,609 thousand GT), mostly Bahri tankers.

supplyRangeKm.note: Educated guess. Large truck fleet and HETs; sustained operations in Yemen ~1,000 km from Riyadh.

draftAnimals.note: Educated guess. Mainly camels; not from FAO data.

nuclearWarheads.note: Saudi Arabia is not listed among the nine nuclear-armed states in the FAS Status of World Nuclear Forces 2026 table. Pakistan defence pact (Sept 2025) and stated intent to match any Iranian bomb are not warheads.

homeDefense.note: Rubric 1.1: vast desert depth and local supply; population support for a dynastic state uncertain (no 1.2).

notes: WARTIME-adjacent snapshot: attacked by Iran in the 2026 Iran war and retaliated (war article), and hit by Houthi missile/drone waves since the Bab al-Mandab crisis (Sept-Oct 2026). asOf 2025 economic data, 2026 order of battle. Population: everything inside ne:SAU incl. ~40% expatriates; the mobilization ratio is set low for that reason. Money in 2011 int$ via derived:ppp-rebase-2011. Counts from Wikipedia inventory tables (Army equipment list, RSAF, Navy, RSADF, SANG); some figures include equipment on order and are flagged. ships_major = frigates (11); corvettes and FAC in ships_minor. Infantry P-role splits are educated guesses (grade D). Paramilitary (24,500, IISS) excluded.
